task.name: groom does not remediate accepted semantic concerns, so an accepted finding is fixed by hand
task.story_text:
---
depends_on:
  - issue-2983
---

## Why

The delegated semantic adjudication spike (theforge#2983) replaces per-revision operator ratification with a loop forge runs itself: evaluate, adjudicate, remediate, re-evaluate, bounded, escalating only what it cannot converge. This issue is the remediation component of that loop. Today an accepted concern only withholds readiness "until the document changes," and changing the document is left to the operator by hand: on hdp#433 on 2026-09-08 the evaluator raised three concerns, all three were accepted, and the body was rewritten by hand and re-submitted. That is the same file → refuse → hand-groom → retry loop `intake.auto_fix` already removed for structural shape, one gate later.

The earlier draft of this issue kept ratification human and only automated the edit after it. That preserved the interruption the feature exists to remove, so it is rewritten to depend on the spike's policy rather than the current one.

## Acceptance criteria

- A concern the adjudication has classified as fixable in the body is remediated by forge as a new document revision, on the same terms as a hand edit: any prior adjudication for the old revision retires with it, and the new revision is evaluated and adjudicated before admission.
- A concern classified as a product decision, and a concern nobody has adjudicated, is never remediated.
- The revision produced is scoped to the concerns being remediated. Parts of the body no concern named are unchanged, byte for byte.
- Remediation is bounded by the loop's retry ceiling. At the ceiling the document escalates rather than being remediated again, and the audit record shows every revision it produced.
- With human ratification selected for the project, remediation of an operator-accepted concern behaves the same way, and the resulting revision awaits the operator's ratification like any other edit.

## Example

```
sprint --issues 433 -> evaluate r1: 3 concerns
                       adjudicate: 3 fixable-in-body
                       remediate:
                         d36deb53  example yields a fractional set count
                                   -> stated the whole-set reduction rule; recomputed the example
                         e11c3613  "trainer-selected" mode undefined
                                   -> defined the mode; added example E and a criterion
                         f55deb8a  exact-slot substitution unspecified
                                   -> declared the fallback order; added example D
                       applied r2 (r1 adjudication retired)
                       evaluate r2: 0 concerns
                       adjudicate: concur
                    -> admitted
```

outcome.message: Preflight: spec is blocked. This issue explicitly depends on issue-2983 (the delegated semantic adjudication spike) for the evaluate/adjudicate/remediate/re-evaluate loop policy, but no such loop, adjudication classification (fixable-in-body vs product-decision vs unadjudicated), retry-ceiling concept, or ratification-mode config exists anywhere in the codebase today. The acceptance criteria assume that policy surface exists to build the remediation component on top of; a dev agent cannot implement remediation against a policy that has not landed.

conventions_soft[0].value: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions

conventions_soft[1].value: Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

conventions_soft[2].value: Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.

conventions_soft[3].value: Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports

conventions_soft[4].value: Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

conventions_soft[5].value: When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it

conventions_soft[6].value: Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

conventions_soft[7].value: Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
